headline: Oil's 3% drop and a Treasury rally open KTBs firmer, then 12,864 contracts of foreign 3Y futures buying extend it: the 10Y falls 3.3bp to 3.942% and the 3Y 2.0bp to 3.716%, with about 1.4bp of the 10Y move explained by Treasuries
summary: KTBs rallied across the curve on the college-entrance-exam day, when markets opened and closed an hour late: the 3Y fell 2.0bp to 3.716% (53rd percentile of its 1-year range), the 10Y 3.3bp to 3.942% (49th) and the 30Y 2.9bp to 4.031%, with the 10Y leading, so 3s10s flattened another 1.3bp to 22.6bp (2nd percentile) and 2s3s inverted to −0.6bp. The 1Y held at 3.636% (90th) and bills stayed at 1-year highs (MSB 91-day 3.206%, CD up 1bp to 3.38%, CP 3.84%), so the market still prices a November 26 hike while buying duration. MSB 2Y fell 2.0bp to 3.740%, 1.8bp over KTB. Spread products lagged the rally: the KDB 3Y fit (32 trades) widened 1.4bp to 25.3bp over KTB (82nd), AAA bank 1Y is 39.8bp over (86th) on a re-fitted curve, AA- 3Y 67.4bp (67th, unchanged) and KEPCO 3Y 40.5bp (77th).
drivers: Foreign futures buying did most of the work

Foreigners bought 12,864 3Y and 5,724 10Y futures after modest buying on Wednesday, and the rally deepened through the afternoon as they added. The KRX 3Y settled 9 ticks higher at 103.55 and the 10Y 37 ticks higher at 108.70. Our basket fair values are 103.64 and 108.69, so the 3Y contract still trades about 9 ticks cheap to its basket and the 10Y is about 1 tick rich, which leaves room for the 3Y to catch up if foreign buying continues.
Treasuries and oil explain under half

WTI fell over 3% to about USD 83 on a second big US crude build, and the US 10Y fell 3bp to 5.07% (par yield) even as the FOMC minutes showed almost all officials saw further hikes as appropriate and Governor Waller argued for 50bp in December. At the 1-year beta of 0.48 that implied −1.4bp for the KTB 10Y; it fell 3.3bp, so about 1.9bp was local. The KTB–UST 10Y gap is −112.8bp, still the widest of the past year (0th percentile).
KOSPI swing did not hurt bonds

KOSPI dipped below 5,000 in the morning, then closed 1.39% higher at 5,137.89 on chip strength and hopes around Anthropic's Nasdaq listing, with foreigners selling about KRW 404bn of stocks for a fifth day. Unlike Wednesday, bonds ignored the equity rebound; USD/KRW fell 3.0 won to 1,330.0 on exporter dollar sales as Korea's cumulative exports passed USD 1tn for the year.

The MOEF said it will not run its non-competitive PD issuance this month given recent supply conditions, a small positive for duration, and will publish the December issuance plan on Nov 26, the same day as the BOK decision. IRS still prices a terminal rate around 3.5% despite the KDI's 3.9% 2027 growth call, so the dot plot is the main event risk.
data: Almost all participants saw further hikes as likely appropriate; held at 3.75–4.00% (10–2)
Net external assets USD 344.8bn (p 64.0bn); net external claims 416.8bn (p 367.8bn)
In line; US 10Y −2bp on the day.
view: Today was split between global and local: Treasuries implied −1.4bp for the 10Y and it fell 3.3bp, so about 1.9bp came from foreign futures buying and cheaper oil; over four weeks the 10Y's −15.5bp splits into +6.9bp from Treasuries (weekly beta 0.63, US 10Y +11bp) and −22.4bp of Korea's own rally.

The rotation signal still reads bond rally (weekly +1.13, daily +1.30), down from +1.62 four weeks ago: margin credit is still 12.9% lower over four weeks and broker deposits down KRW 5.7tn, which offsets KOSPI's climb back to 5,138.

With a hike priced and IRS holding a 3.5% terminal, I expect the 10Y to trade 3.88–4.02% into the BOK and the curve to stay flat (3s10s 22.6bp, 2nd percentile; 2s3s inverted), so I stay out of steepeners until after the dot plot.
Book: keep the 10Y long (average 3.975%, now +3.3bp outright and about +5bp hedged), keep the half-size KDB 3Y overweight (25.3bp, 0.4bp against us) and wait for the 30s50s switch to back up to 0bp.

Hedging the rotation view against Treasuries remains the better way to hold it: weekly hedged rally calls were right 68% of the time and sell-off calls 69% (Sharpe 1.34, worst drawdown −26bp) against 52%, 57%, 0.93 and −36bp outright; a hawkish dot plot on Nov 26 or a hot US print are the main risks.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 1.3bp to 3.722%, 79th percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.40%), while the 1Y held at 3.636% (90th). 2s3s inverted to −0.6bp (0th percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s is 8.6bp (2nd). MSB 91-day (3.206%) and CD (3.38%) sit at 1-year highs and price a hike to 3.25% on Nov 26; Hana and Citi see 3.5% as the end point.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (7.8bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 1.3bp to 22.6bp (2nd percentile, average 39.4bp, 1-year low 20.8bp) as foreign futures buying pulled the 10Y down more than the 3Y. The 3s5s10s fly is −3.4bp (14th, average 4.3bp), so the belly stays rich. Our earlier steepener was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat: KOSPI closed at 5,138, below the 5,300 re-entry trigger. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only on a KOSPI close above 5,300 or after a BOK hike; target 32bp, stop 19bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.942% sits at the 49th percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.93%). Treasuries implied −1.4bp and the 10Y fell 3.3bp, so the hedged long gained about 2bp today. The new 10Y (26-13) still trades about 7bp rich to the fitted curve, the richest liquid line; 25-8 in the 4Y area is the cheapest (+4bp).
buckets.call: Long, average 3.975%, stop 4.10%, target 3.85%; hold against about 0.5 × US 10Y. Open, +3.3bp outright, about +5bp hedged.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s rose 0.7bp to −2.4bp as the 30Y outperformed the 50Y, two days after our 30Y-into-50Y switch hit target (+5.6bp). The spread is at the 86th percentile (average −9.0bp), so the 50Y stays cheap against history. The 10s20s30s fly rose 1.0bp to 14.7bp (82nd), with the 20Y lagging.
buckets.call: Closed at target, +5.6bp. Re-enter the 30Y-into-50Y switch on a back-up to 0bp; target −5bp, stop +2.5bp.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: With 32 trades the KDB fit puts the 3Y 25.3bp over KTB, 82nd percentile (average 19.6bp), 1.4bp wider as KTBs rallied faster than policy-bank paper. The 1Y fit is 25.1bp over (44th) and KOFIA's 1Y quote 24.0bp (44th). IBK 1Y is 32.2bp over on 15 trades (75th); KEXIM jumped 11.5bp to 36.3bp on only 5 trades, so treat it as low confidence.
buckets.call: Keep: overweight KDB 3Y vs KTB 3Y from 24.9bp, now 25.3bp (−0.4bp); target 18bp, stop 30bp. Add the second half if it holds below 26bp after the BOK.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: The bank curve was re-fitted on 45 trades and now puts the 1Y 39.8bp over KTB, 86th percentile (average 30.9bp), against 36.0bp we showed yesterday; the 3Y is 27.1bp over (41st). CD rose 1bp to 3.38% and CP held at 3.84%, so CP–CD narrowed to 46bp (89th, average 29bp) and CD–MSB91 widened to 17bp (30th).
buckets.call: No change: revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp; prefer the 1Y over the 3Y if adding.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 1.9bp to 4.390%, in step with the KTB 3Y, so the spread held at 67.4bp (67th percentile, average 61.8bp). KEPCO 3Y is 40.5bp over (77th, average 34.9bp) and BBB- minus AA- 583bp (77th). Credit kept pace with the rally but is not tightening.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI regains 5,300; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US jobless claims and Philly Fed (Nov 19 US time), Korea October PPI (Nov 20), Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 23, the BOK decision, dot plot and new forecasts plus the MOEF December issuance plan on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced), and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; KTBs take about 0.45–0.5bp per Treasury bp on the day.
